not_validated.item: Individual rise and set times on real terrain
not_validated.reason: The long-term shares of lit and Earth-visible time agree with the published LOLA maps on terrain of the same resolution; of the two checks against dated images one agrees and one fails its criterion; and no independent source gives the time of a sunrise or sunset at a point on real terrain. Where an event is set by terrain closer than about 1 km, the elevation grid limits its accuracy.
Every terrain check on this card uses LOLA elevation data on both sides. The data stream checks the georeferencing of the LOLA files separately.

not_validated.item: Exact rise and set times at a real lander
not_validated.reason: No source examined for Blue Ghost Mission 1, Chandrayaan-3, SLIM, IM-1 or IM-2 prints a sunrise or sunset clock time for the landing site. Operational records (hours of daylight, expected wake-up date) only bound the computed events from one side.

Both ends of the link geometry agree with Horizons. The windows built from them, the station elevation limits as single numbers (no azimuth-dependent masks), and anything about link budget, multipath or scheduling have not been compared with an external source.

not_validated.item: Earth rise and set against an independent source
not_validated.reason: Horizons does not state which point of the Earth's disc its rise and set refer to; only the Earth's direction and size are validated.

Eclipses of the Sun by the Earth are computed for an opaque Earth without atmosphere and checked against one published eclipse. The light that the Earth's atmosphere refracts into the shadow, and any measured power curve of a lander, are not modelled or compared.

limits: Near the lunar poles the terrain horizon, not the ephemeris, sets the accuracy of an event time: a horizon error of 0.01 deg can move an event by many minutes. The terrain checks on this card test long-term shares and two dated images, not event times.
The external reference (Horizons) and the core use JPL ephemerides of the same family; an error common to both would not show.

Thresholds marked as written in the acceptance test were committed in the same commit as the code they test; the thresholds of the comparisons with external sources have commits of their own that predate the data or the computation, as listed above.
The lander and eclipse comparisons are not blind: earlier research had compared some of the published values with Horizons.
